correctness.rationale: With a=alpha-1>0 the displayed law equals a mixture of negative-binomial counts of shapes a and a+1 at the same success probability t/(1+t), weighted t/(1+t) and 1/(1+t). This recovers the positive, normalized mass. The gamma recurrence gives the neighboring ratio R_j with b=a(t+2). Clearing its positive denominators shows R_{j+1}-R_j has sign opposite the monic H(j)=j^2+(2b-2t-1)j+b(b-t)-2(t+1). The first-index value H(0) has its unique positive shape root at a_c(t); at b=t+1/2, where the linear coefficient vanishes, H(0)=-(6t+7)/4. Thus above or at the boundary the linear coefficient is positive, and H(j)>H(0) for j>0. Below the boundary H(0)<0 and its two real roots have opposite sign, giving exactly one curvature transition and at most one flat step. For the peak count, the sign numerator of R_j-1 is a strictly concave quadratic with leading coefficient -t, so the positive indices are a single finite block; zeros allow ties but no additional separated peak. In particular, when the positive block is empty, two integer zeros must be adjacent if both occur, so any weak interior peak is confined to one equality plateau. For a=2/3 the exact rational endpoint tests give R_0<1<R_1 and R_2<1 across the stated interval. Decreasing forward differences of the concave numerator then give R_j<1 for all j>=2. The only global candidates are 0 and 2. Their probability difference has the sign of minus the cubic, which is strictly increasing in t>0 and changes sign inside the rational bracket. This proves the unique switch and excludes all other counts at the tie, without using finite samples to make an infinite assertion.
residual_risks: The theorem is about the full count PMF for alpha>1 and t>0, not a hazard theorem or a regression performance claim. Peak counting allows adjacent equalities; strict decreases are asserted only where the ratio inequality is strict.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Sharing the two modal indices is not equality of laws or of thresholds. The exponentiated discrete Lindley law with a fixed q has probabilities with a linear-geometric leading tail (exponentiating the CDF multiplies its leading survivor by a constant). value.rationale: Replacing a blanket shape assertion for an actually used count model with a sharp full-domain curvature test is substantive. The exact separated tied modes and strict switch show a qualitative failure of unimodality, not merely failure of a sufficient test or a numerical irregularity. The witness and the peak bound are directly useful for modal interpretation without making unsupported claims about reliability or estimation.
residual_risks: The explicit switch is a proved parameter slice, not a complete two-dimensional list of all coexistence curves.
